data.title: Avoid NaN photon position errors for clusters without a position
data.author: davidlange6
data.body:
positionCovFromAngles divides by the distance of the cluster position from the origin. Delphes' DualReadoutCalorimeter can produce EFlow photons at (0, 0, 0): towers that only have track hits never get a position, and a fluctuation of the calorimeter energy can make them a neutral-excess photon. For those, all six entries of Cluster.positionError were NaN (about 1 in 64k photons in e+e- -> Z with the IDEA card; seen with the current key4hep nightly as well).

Return an all-zero covariance when there is no impact point, as the error is undefined there.

data.title: perf(build): only look for the Python interpreter in DD4hepConfig
data.author: chrisburr
data.body:
I've been looking at speeding up the cmake configuration time in LHCb and I found that `FIND_PACKAGE(Python)` was being called many times. This ends up being slow due to `python-config` being called several time and the build we use of Python has a high startup overhead.

This ends up saving ~1.5 seconds on the builds I was benchmarking with:

|       | Baseline      | Patched       |
|-------|---------------|---------------|
| Rec   | 18.8 / 16.4 s | 15.1 / 15.2 s |
| Moore | 17.0 / 16.1 s | 14.2 / 14.7 s |


BEGINRELEASENOTES

- DD4hepConfig: look only for the Python interpreter when DD4hep was built without Geant4 (and not the development component)

data.author: jmcarcell

data.title: Merge dependabot's updates by themselves once CI passes
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
Dependabot's pull requests now merge by themselves once CI passes, as in key4hep/k4Bench.

- `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml` (the same as k4Bench's): on each pull request opened by dependabot, it enables auto-merge with squash.
- Repository settings, already changed: **Allow auto-merge** is on, and a ruleset **Require CI on main** requires the checks `lint`, `test` and `dashboard` before anything merges into `main` (bypass: the repository's maintainer, as in k4Bench). Without required checks, auto-merge would merge at once instead of waiting for CI.
- README: says that dependency updates merge once CI passes.

All three required jobs run on every pull request to `main`, so none of them can block a merge by being skipped.

data.title: A stage waiting for its twin holds no worker; a resume reuses every level
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
A stage that waits for an identical one no longer holds a worker, and a resume reuses what every level of a nested study made. The number of trials proposed at once is unchanged, and now an explicit rule.

## Problems found

1. **A waiting stage held its slots.** When a stage with the same signature was already running, the duplicate waited for it, but the scheduler had already counted its slots. So it held one worker, or `numberOfThreads` of them, while doing nothing. With two samples, a shared `gamma` simulation and each candidate's own `pion`, 4 workers ran 1.7 simulations on average; the rest were held by waiting duplicates.
